purpose: Evaluation only; never ingest these questions, answers or source-ID labels as scenario evidence.
judging_policy: required_source_ids identify evidence needed for the expected answer, not substring answers. A retrieval-only run must report source recall separately from answer correctness and abstention. Human acceptance or an explicitly configured judge is required for semantic answer scores.

questions.query: Does adding a query string to a Link reliably force a fresh server result on every visit?
questions.answer: No universal guarantee. Fredkiss3 first reported a promising experiment, then qualified it: same-segment URLs can be cached after initial visits; random values risk hydration issues and stable IDs can still be cached.
forbidden_claims: The first experiment is a documented universal guarantee.

questions.query: Did the new unit tests mean the maintainers had decided to keep the disputed navigation behavior permanently?
questions.answer: No. Tim explained the tests cover existing behavior and help development; the right behavior and mutation interaction were still under discussion.
forbidden_claims: Unit tests ratified the behavior as permanent product policy.

questions.query: Was the session drift in the reviewed reproduction attributed only to the router cache?
questions.answer: No. Tim identified module-scoped state shared between requests and a session-changing side effect in layout rendering in that reproduction. This does not settle every other stale-data report.
forbidden_claims: All stale-data reports were caused by the same application bug.

questions.query: If I turn off Link prefetch, can I assume repeat navigation avoids stale client data across the versions discussed?
questions.answer: No. The reply distinguishes the older workaround, including 13.3.1, from newer cache reuse. PR 48383 describes reuse even with prefetch disabled. The behavior is version-specific.
forbidden_claims: prefetch=false always disables the client router cache.

questions.query: Who actually tried the proposed older release, and what did they report after trying it?
questions.answer: grantmagdanz reported that downgrading to 13.3.1 gave their application the desired behavior and accepted slower navigation. That is a local confirmation, not proof for every app.
forbidden_claims: zuinqstudio-admin had already verified the downgrade.

questions.query: Can I treat the pageTTL code shown in the discussion as an official configuration API?
questions.answer: No. Fredkiss3 explicitly identified it as an imagined shape for a possible future option and said the official API could differ.
forbidden_claims: pageTTL is a supported Next.js export in the cited releases.
The sketch is an approved maintainer API.

questions.query: What was the proposed custom navigation workaround, and what costs or counterexamples were reported?
questions.answer: Fredkiss3 proposed push followed by refresh inside startTransition, with server round trips even for static pages. zuinqstudio-admin reported two refreshes/API fetches in their app and only intended to try a downgrade.
forbidden_claims: The custom link has no extra requests.
The second user confirmed the downgrade had worked.

questions.query: Should we discard all comments labeled outdated because the maintainers said their technical content was obsolete?
questions.answer: No. Tim explicitly said the label tracked comments he had read and categorized; it was not a judgment that the content was obsolete.
forbidden_claims: The outdated label is evidence of technical invalidation.

questions.query: At the morning update on August 15, was the explanatory write-up already published and approved?
questions.answer: No. It was close to completion and still needed review by sebmarkbage later that day. The selected snapshot has not yet published it.
forbidden_claims: The morning update contains the published discussion link.
The write-up was already approved in that update.

questions.query: Where did the maintainer direct people next, and what did they say that resource was for?
questions.answer: Tim linked discussion 54075 to explain mutation and routing behavior and gather feedback about the cache interval. He asked readers to study it before replying. This was not a release announcement.
forbidden_claims: The discussion shipped a cache-disabling API.

questions.query: Does closing the original issue establish that all affected applications were fixed?
questions.answer: No. Tim said he would close and lock the issue to move the explanation, questions and continuing resolution to the new discussion.
forbidden_claims: Closure means every report was fixed and verified.

questions.query: What exact officially released option did the team ultimately ship to set the router cache lifetime to zero, and in which release?
questions.answer: The selected corpus does not establish an ultimately shipped option or release. It contains a hypothetical API, possible follow-up work, and a later discussion collecting feedback. Abstain from naming an option or release.
forbidden_claims: The selected evidence establishes a later release number.
